row.evidence: Asana's pricing page lists User provisioning (SCIM) under the Enterprise plan ("Contact sales for pricing", "Everything in Advanced, plus"), and the developer docs say only Service Accounts in Enterprise domains can access SCIM endpoints.
row.notes: Unchanged from June: SCIM and SAML both start at Enterprise (Contact Sales); Starter $10.99 and Advanced $24.99 per user/mo billed annually. Google and Microsoft sign-in are on all paid plans but are not SAML. SCIM needs an Enterprise-only Service Account token. SCIM deprovisioning removes the member (no recoverable deactivated state); reactivation and team deletion via SCIM are not supported. Audit Log API is Enterprise+ or Enterprise with the Compliance management add-on.

auth.token_source: Admin Console > Apps > Service accounts > Add Service Account (scoped permission: User provisioning (SCIM))

deprovision.data_retained: Member is removed ('zombified'); there is no recoverable deactivated state. Their assigned public tasks go into an auto-generated 'Previously assigned tasks' project owned by a super admin; ownership of projects, portfolios and dashboards is not transferred; private resources must be made public before removal to keep access.

roles.how: SCIM 'roles' attribute whose value is an RBAC role ID taken from the Admin Console; 'licenses' attribute assigns Asana licenses.

limitations.text: Only Service Accounts in Enterprise domains can call SCIM; Service accounts are Enterprise/Enterprise+ only and not available to divisions.
Reactivating members and deleting teams are not supported; there is no DELETE /Groups endpoint documented.
Deprovisioning (active=false, DELETE, or Okta deactivate) deletes/removes the member rather than suspending them.
GET /Users does not return guests; guests are managed only in the Admin Console, and provisioned emails must match the organization's domain.
name.givenName/name.familyName are not supported in PATCH; use name.formatted.
preferredLanguage is applied only at creation (per the Okta section).
Asana's own help article says Google Workspace SCIM needs contact with the account executive or support, though Google's admin help documents Asana autoprovisioning.
The live help article still contains an unresolved internal '[VERIFY before publishing ...]' note about the exact admin role and tier required.

endpoints.purpose: List users in a workspace or organization (max 2000)
Add (invite) a user to a workspace or organization
Remove a user from a workspace or organization (admin; same as SCIM DELETE when called with a Service Account token)
Add a user to a team
Remove a user from a team
List RBAC roles in a workspace

audit_log_api.plan: Enterprise+ (or Enterprise with the Compliance management add-on); Service Account token required

rate_limits.text: Per token: 150 requests/min on free domains, 1,500/min on paid domains; also concurrency and cost limits.

limitations.text: Service Account tokens (organization-wide access, required for SCIM, audit log and workspace events APIs) are Enterprise/Enterprise+ only; PAT/OAuth calls act as an individual user.
Workspace events API is Enterprise+ or Enterprise with the Compliance Management add-on.

okta.notes: OIN page marks SAML, SWA, SCIM and Create/Update/Deactivate/Group Push/Group Linking as checked (read from page markup; the visible text lists every capability label).

onelogin.notes: OneLogin's own connector page could not be loaded (bot challenge); facts come from Asana's help centre.

open_questions: SCIM docs do not describe pagination (startIndex/count) or a maximum page size for GET /Users or GET /Groups.
Docs do not say whether SAML sign-in creates accounts just-in-time.
Docs do not say whether SCIM deprovisioning revokes active sessions.
No custom (non-listed) SCIM attributes are documented; unclear whether they are rejected or ignored.
Bulk and /Me SCIM endpoints are not mentioned in the SCIM docs.
Service Account token expiry is not documented.
SCIM-specific rate limits are not documented separately from the general API limits.
No REST endpoint for assigning RBAC roles or licenses to a user was seen (SCIM supports both); not verified whether PUT /users/{user_gid} can.
Enterprise seat minimum and price are not public.
OneLogin's connector page (onelogin.com/connector/asana) returned a bot challenge and could not be loaded.
Whether bulk CSV member import is limited to particular plans was not shown on the help page.
